intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HECW2 gene.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123) is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. Features include global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia and seizures, which may be drug-resistant. Some patients also have microcephaly, failure to thrive, severe gastroesophageal reflux, and brain imaging abnormalities such as cerebral and cerebellar atrophy (Krami et al., 2022; Rodriguez-Garcia et al., 2022; Dehghanzad et al., 2025).

paragraphs.text: Using whole-exome sequencing, Rodriguez-Garcia et al. (2022) identified a homozygous deletion-insertion in the HECW2 gene (g.197092814_197092824delinsC) in a Caucasian girl with DEE123. The variant disrupted the splice donor site of intron 22. It caused skipping of exon 22 (r.3766_3917+1del), which led to an in-frame deletion in the protein (p.Leu1256_Trp1306del). In functional studies, RNA expression was increased twofold, but protein expression was reduced by 60%. The authors suggested a partial loss-of-function mechanism.

paragraphs.text: Using whole-exome sequencing, Dehghanzad et al. (2025) identified a homozygous 1-bp insertion in the HECW2 gene (c.3601_3602insT) in a girl of consanguineous Afghan descent with DEE123. The insertion was predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Tyr1201LeufsTer7). Sanger sequencing confirmed the variant, and both unaffected parents were heterozygous carriers. In silico analyses supported pathogenicity. The authors suggested that the variant likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. This loss-of-function mechanism would be distinct from the one implicated for missense variants that cause the autosomal dominant disorder.
